entities.summary:
The Azerbaijan National Academy of Sciences (ANAS), established in 1945, serves as the principal scientific institution of Azerbaijan, located in the capital city of Baku. This academy plays a crucial role in the advancement of research and education in Azerbaijan, significantly influencing the nation’s academic landscape and contributing to the cultural and intellectual heritage of the region. Prominent figures such as academician Mahmoud Abdullayev and physicist Lotfi Zadeh have been associated with the institution, aiding in its development and international collaboration efforts.

Since its inception, ANAS has been actively involved in various scientific disciplines, including natural sciences, social sciences, and humanities. The academy has established numerous research institutes and laboratories, fostering advancements in fields like physics, mathematics, and biology. Notably, the academy has published significant research findings and has been a participant in international conferences, positioning Azerbaijani science on the global stage. In 1962, it hosted the International Symposium on Quantum Electronics, underscoring its commitment to engage with global scientific communities.

The legacy of ANAS extends beyond its immediate contributions to science and education; it has also influenced the post-Soviet scientific landscape, fostering independence in research and innovation within Azerbaijan. The institution's commitment to scientific excellence has paved the way for future generations of researchers and has contributed to the development of a national identity rooted in scientific achievement. Furthermore, ANAS has established partnerships with various international organizations, enhancing its ability to contribute to global scientific discourse.
